In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of cell wounding, repair, and adaptation.
the mechanisms of plasma membrane wounding and repair.
the mechanisms of cell wounding in the context of lung injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most appropriate experimental system for the study of cell wounding should be based upon the cell type and the nature of the injury.
there is no perfect experimental model to simulate in vivo cell wounding.
the experimental models of cell damage and repair are useful tools for understanding the mechanisms of cell wounding in vivo and for developing therapeutic strategies for cell injury and repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell injury in vitro, in general, is not a simple process and that the mechanisms by which the plasma membrane integrity is restored are not fully understood.
cell wounding is a dynamic and complex process that depends on cell type, the type of insult, and the size and nature the injury.
alveolar type II cells can survive a large injury, but only if they can rapidly repair their plasma membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nature of the wounding event can influence the outcome of the response.
the alveolar epithelial cells are highly sensitive to cell wounding.
the size of the wound, the cell type and the experimental conditions used to study cell wounding can have a dramatic effect on the ability of cells to repair their plasma membrane.
